From: HM Treasury , Ministry of Defence , Defence Nuclear Enterprise , The Rt Hon John Healey MP and The Rt Hon Wes Streeting MP Published: 28 September 2026 Government backs British shipyards with multi-billion pound investment in three major maritime projects to strengthen national security, support skilled jobs and drive growth in every part of the UK. Chancellor confirms three new floating docks for the Royal Navy’s submarine service at HM Naval Base Clyde will be built in Britain supporting Britain’s defence industrial base and securing key sovereign capabilities. New marine research vessel to be built in a British shipyard, backing coastal communities, sustainable fishing and long-term economic growth. British shipyards will be at the heart of two major maritime projects worth billions of pounds, helping to create high-skilled jobs, drive growth and strengthen the UK’s long-term industrial and national security capabilities. Chancellor John Healey will pledge a “new age of industrialisation” for Britain today as he confirms the multi-billion pound projects will be built by British workers, supporting jobs and a pipeline of small British businesses. Healey will confirm that the Royal Navy’s submarine service at HM Naval Base Clyde will receive three new floating docks - known as Programme Euston - through a UK-only competition, in light of their importance to national security and sovereign British industry. The new facilities will provide crucial maintenance for the UK’s current and future fleet of nuclear submarines, allowing essential inspections, upgrades and repairs to be carried out. In addition to this, the Chancellor has also committed to funding for a new marine research vessel to help protect our seas. Set to be operational in the early 2030s, it will continue the delivery of core research on our seas and oceans, replacing the current vessel which is nearing the end of its life. The evidence it collects will help ensure the security of our seas, support sustainable fishing and give coastal communities confidence that fish stocks are being managed for the future. Both projects will be delivered by UK companies, as part of a greater focus on how government spends taxpayers’ money to boost national security whilst also supporting British jobs and growth in local communities. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said: “Britain has a proud shipbuilding heritage, and every pound of this strategic investment in a critical sector is backing British jobs on the Clyde and businesses across the UK, supporting growth in every postcode. “By backing British shipyards, we are not only boosting national security but also securing resilience in the industries that will drive growth today while building the capabilities the country needs for the future.” Defence Secretary, Wes Streeting said: “Defence spending should make Britain stronger in every sense. That means backing British by buying British wherever our industry can deliver. “HM Naval Base Clyde is at the heart of our submarine service. Programme Euston will modernise it for decades to come, while backing British shipyards, workers and engineering. “That is defence driving the reindustrialisation of Britain and strengthening our sovereign capability.” Share this page The following links open in a new tab Share on Facebook (opens in new tab) Share on X (opens in new tab) Is this page useful? live_web_research.page_text: John Healey pledges 'new age of industrialisation' with UK-only shipbuilding contracts - Chichester News Wednesday, October 7, 2026 News Chichester West Sussex Money Property Travel Business Politics Sport Cricket Football Rugby Running Tennis More Culture Features Council Charity Community Crime Education Health & Public Services Lifestyle Transport No Result View All Result News Chichester West Sussex Money Property Travel Business Politics Sport Cricket Football Rugby Running Tennis More Culture Features Council Charity Community Crime Education Health & Public Services Lifestyle Transport No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home Business John Healey pledges ‘new age of industrialisation’ with UK-only shipbuilding contracts by Carl Eldridge September 28, 2026 in Business Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 0 0 Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on Whatsapp Share on Telegram Chancellor John Healey has pledged a “new age of industrialisation” for the United Kingdom, announcing significant government backing for two major maritime projects to be built exclusively in British shipyards. Speaking at the Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, the Chancellor outlined a strategy intended to secure sovereign industrial capability while modernising the nation’s naval and research infrastructure. The investment focuses on two key pillars: a fleet of new floating docks for the Royal Navy’s submarine service and a state-of-the-art marine research vessel. RELATED POSTS UK Insurance Fraud Hits £1.34 Billion Despite Fewer Total Cases The Rise of the Junior SIPP: How a £100 Monthly Saving Strategy Secures Retirement at 57 Central to the announcement is Programme Euston, a project to construct three new floating docks at HM Naval Base Clyde (Faslane). These docks are essential for the maintenance and operational readiness of the UK’s submarine fleet. In a move designed to bolster domestic manufacturing, the government confirmed that the contracts for Programme Euston will be restricted to a UK-only competitive tender process. Contracts for the new vessels will be restricted to a UK-only competitive tender process. Alongside the naval infrastructure, the government is committing at least £115 million to the construction of a new marine research vessel. According to the UK Defence Journal , these submarine docks are being reserved for British shipyards to ensure the work supports the domestic economy. The new research vessel is expected to become operational in the early 2030s. Like the floating docks, it will be subject to a UK-only tender process, ensuring the design and construction phases support skilled jobs across the country’s historic shipbuilding hubs. Industry leaders and shipbuilding organisations are expected to monitor the upcoming tender timelines closely. By restricting these high-value contracts to domestic bidders, the government aims to provide long-term certainty for a sector that has faced significant international competition in recent decades. The Chancellor’s address emphasised that this “industrialisation” approach is not merely about procurement, but about maintaining the skills and technology required to protect British interests at sea. Further details regarding the specific tender dates and the breakdown of regional job creation are expected to be released as the procurement phases for Programme Euston and the research vessel begin later this year. Title: A Breakthrough in Quantum Computing: IBM's Quantum Conditional Gate Demonstrated

IBM has successfully demonstrated a quantum conditional gate, a crucial component in the development of quantum computers, according to a recent research paper published by the company.

The quantum conditional gate, also known as the controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate, is a two-qubit quantum gate that performs a specific operation based on the state of the first qubit. This gate is essential for implementing quantum algorithms that require conditional operations, such as Shor's algorithm for factoring large numbers.

The IBM team's achievement marks a significant step forward in the field of quantum computing. The CNOT gate is one of the building blocks for more complex quantum circuits, and its successful demonstration indicates that IBM is making progress towards creating a scalable quantum computer.

However, it is important to note that the research paper does not provide specific details about the performance or capabilities of the demonstrated CNOT gate. The paper also does not mention the number of qubits involved, the error rate, or the coherence time of the qubits. These factors are crucial for assessing the practicality and potential of the developed technology.

IBM's achievement in demonstrating a quantum conditional gate adds to the growing body of evidence suggesting that quantum computing is moving closer to reality. As more companies and research institutions continue to invest in and develop quantum technologies, we can expect to see more breakthroughs in the near future.

In conclusion, IBM's successful demonstration of a quantum conditional gate is a significant milestone in the development of quantum computers. While more work is needed to fully understand the capabilities and limitations of the demonstrated gate, this achievement underscores the potential of quantum computing and the ongoing efforts to create a scalable quantum computer.
